result:
I’d make a safe, dignified childhood universal.

Enough food. A home without terror. Someone reliable who cares whether you come back. Time to learn and play without having to earn your right to exist.

Not because that would solve everything, but because so much suffering begins before a person has any power to refuse it—and then echoes through the rest of their life, sometimes into other people’s lives.

That’s the change I’d choose: fewer people having to spend adulthood recovering from the beginning.
